name: Median Nerve
pathway: Travels with brachial artery, passes through cubital fossa, enters forearm between heads of pronator teres, runs through carpal tunnel into hand.
clinical: Compression in carpal tunnel causes carpal tunnel syndrome; weakness in thumb opposition and forearm pronation.

name: Ulnar Nerve
pathway: Passes posterior to medial epicondyle of humerus, continues along ulnar side of forearm into hand.
clinical: Injury at elbow or wrist can cause "claw hand" and sensory loss in medial hand.

name: Axillary Nerve
pathway: Exits axilla through quadrangular space with posterior circumflex humeral artery, wraps around surgical neck of humerus.
clinical: Injury can occur with shoulder dislocation or humeral surgical neck fracture, causing deltoid paralysis and sensory loss over deltoid.

name: Suprascapular Nerve
pathway: Passes through suprascapular notch under the superior transverse scapular ligament to supply supraspinatus and infraspinatus.
clinical: Compression at the notch can cause weakness in shoulder abduction and external rotation.

name: Musculocutaneous Nerve
pathway: Pierces coracobrachialis, travels between biceps brachii and brachialis, continues as lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.
clinical: Injury results in weakened elbow flexion and forearm supination with sensory loss along the lateral forearm.

name: Radial Nerve
pathway: Runs in radial groove of humerus, traverses lateral intermuscular septum, divides into superficial and deep branches near lateral epicondyle.
clinical: Injury in the radial groove causes wrist drop and sensory loss over dorsum of hand.

name: Anterior Interosseous Nerve
pathway: Branch of the median nerve coursing along the anterior interosseous membrane to the deep flexor compartment.
clinical: Lesion produces pinch weakness (OK sign) due to loss of thumb and index finger flexion.

name: Posterior Interosseous Nerve
pathway: Deep branch of radial nerve passing through supinator to supply posterior forearm extensors.
clinical: Compression in the supinator (radial tunnel) causes finger and thumb extension weakness without sensory loss.

name: Lateral Pectoral Nerve
pathway: Arises from lateral cord of brachial plexus, passes medially to pierce clavipectoral fascia reaching pectoralis major.
clinical: Lesion reduces shoulder flexion and adduction strength from the clavicular head of pectoralis major.

name: Medial Pectoral Nerve
pathway: Originates from medial cord, pierces pectoralis minor to reach and supply pectoralis major.
clinical: Injury weakens scapular depression and shoulder adduction contributed by pectoralis major and minor.

name: Upper Subscapular Nerve
pathway: Branches from posterior cord, enters proximal subscapularis on its anterior surface.
clinical: Injury decreases initial shoulder medial rotation strength.

name: Lower Subscapular Nerve
pathway: Branches from posterior cord, descends along the subscapularis to innervate its inferior portion and teres major.
clinical: Damage impairs shoulder medial rotation and adduction from subscapularis and teres major.

name: Deep Branch of Ulnar Nerve
pathway: Passes through Guyon's canal, diving deep to supply most intrinsic hand muscles.
clinical: Compression in Guyon's canal causes weakness in interossei and hypothenar muscles with sensory sparing.

name: Recurrent Branch of Median Nerve
pathway: Emerges after the carpal tunnel to supply thenar muscles.
clinical: Injury during carpal tunnel release leads to loss of thumb opposition and abduction.

name: Long Thoracic Nerve
pathway: Descends along lateral thoracic wall, superficial to serratus anterior.
clinical: Injury leads to winged scapula due to paralysis of serratus anterior.
